findings.summary: Lag and rolling features (shift(1), shift(7), rolling 7 mean) are computed across the whole frame instead of per store_id, so a store's first rows take lag values from the previous store and dropna only removes the first 7 rows overall.
Row-based shifts assume the data is sorted by date and has no gaps; with unsorted or missing dates, sales_lag7 isn't the same weekday last week and can leak future values (target leakage).
test_lag_features uses only a single store, so it cannot catch the cross-store lag bug.
test_calendar_features passes only by coincidence because the first 7 rows are dropped, so out.loc[0] is 2026-01-08 (also a Thursday) and it no longer checks 2026-01-01.
